newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: FORECAST-EMU to boost Austrian growth, employment.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-EMU to boost Austrian growth, employment.

text.p: Austria's WIFO research institute said on Friday European economic and monetary union (EMU) would boost the economy in the medium term, but warned a big starting group could trigger higher inflation and weaken the euro.
"Austria could expect gross domestic product to grow by 2.25 percent in real terms and employment to rise by about 0.66 percent", WIFO said in a statement released on Friday.
The findings were based on the assumption that EMU would start with 11 countries, WIFO said.
It would be better for the integration process within the European Union (EU) to start with a bigger group, the institute noted, but warned there were economic risks attached.

"Inflation and interest rates would rise in hard currency countries while they would fall in countries with weaker currencies," WIFO said, adding that the prospective single currency would have to be devalued against the dollar.
"In a large EMU the euro would be devalued in the medium term by 6.75 percent against the dollar", WIFO stated.
At present it looked more likely that EMU would begin with a small number of countries -- the hard currency countries including Austria, WIFO said.
"This would fulfil best the idea of an optimal currency area and guarantee stability and trust in the euro", it noted.
WIFO said that growth and employment in the smaller group would lag behind but declined to give any figures.
The institute forecast benefits for the economy through the stabilisation of cross rates, competition in financial services and lower transaction costs.

There was certainly potential for economic growth, WIFO added. To achieve this goal the EU would have to co-ordinate national budget policies with a central currency policy. -- Christian Gutlederer +43 1 531 12 275
